subject: Reasoning
topic: Logical Sequence — Ordering by Size, Hierarchy, Process Stages and Evolutionary Development (W13 B1)

questions.stem: Arrange the following in increasing order of size in biology: 1. Organ, 2. Atom, 3. Cell, 4. Molecule, 5. Tissue. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Biological organisation from smallest to largest: Atom (2) < Molecule (4) < Cell (3) < Tissue (5) < Organ (1). This is a fundamental biology sequence: atoms form molecules (chemical level) → molecules organise into cells (cellular level) → cells group into tissues (tissue level) → tissues form organs (organ level). Trap: Option B (2,3,4,5,1) puts cell before molecule — wrong; a cell is composed of molecules, so molecule < cell. Option C starts with molecule before atom — atoms are smaller than molecules.

questions.stem: Arrange the following in the order of life cycle of a butterfly: 1. Adult butterfly, 2. Egg, 3. Pupa (chrysalis), 4. Larva (caterpillar). Which is the correct sequence?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Butterfly metamorphosis (complete/holometabolous): Egg (2) → Larva/Caterpillar (4) → Pupa/Chrysalis (3) → Adult butterfly (1). Four distinct stages: the larva hatches from the egg, then forms a pupa and transforms inside, finally emerging as an adult. This is a standard 4-stage complete metamorphosis. Trap: Option B (2,3,4,1) puts pupa before larva — wrong; the caterpillar (larva) must come before it forms a pupa.

questions.stem: Arrange the following in ascending order of military rank: 1. Brigadier, 2. Colonel, 3. Captain, 4. Major, 5. Lieutenant. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Indian Army officer ranks (ascending): Lieutenant (5) < Captain (3) < Major (4) < Colonel (2) < Brigadier (1). Full sequence for reference: Second Lt. < Lieutenant < Captain < Major < Lieutenant Colonel < Colonel < Brigadier < Major General < Lieutenant General < General < Field Marshal. Trap: Option B starts with Captain before Lieutenant — wrong; Lieutenant is junior to Captain.

questions.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of cotton processing from raw material to cloth: 1. Weaving, 2. Ginning, 3. Spinning, 4. Cotton plant, 5. Dyeing. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Cotton-to-fabric process: Cotton plant (4) → Ginning (2) [separating cotton fibre from seeds] → Spinning (3) [converting fibres into yarn/thread] → Weaving (1) [interlacing yarn into cloth] → Dyeing (5) [colouring the fabric]. Each step logically follows the previous: you gin before spinning (can't spin unseparated seeds), spin before weaving (need yarn to weave), weave before dyeing (need fabric to dye). Trap: Option B puts spinning before ginning — wrong; you must first gin the cotton to get clean fibre.

questions.stem: Arrange the following historical events related to India's independence in chronological order: 1. Quit India Movement, 2. Dandi March, 3. Partition and Independence, 4. Formation of Indian National Army (INA). Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Chronological order: Dandi March (2) — 1930 → Quit India Movement (1) — August 1942 → Formation of INA (4) — 1943 (Subhash Chandra Bose formally reorganised it in 1943) → Partition and Independence (3) — 1947. Key dates: 1930 (salt march), 1942 (Quit India), 1943 (INA), 1947 (independence). Trap: Option B puts Quit India before Dandi March — Dandi March (1930) preceded Quit India (1942) by 12 years.

questions.stem: Arrange the following local administrative units in India from smallest to largest: 1. District, 2. State, 3. Taluk/Tehsil, 4. Village, 5. Gram Panchayat. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Ascending administrative hierarchy: Village (4) < Gram Panchayat (5) [group of villages] < Taluk/Tehsil (3) [group of panchayats] < District (1) [group of taluks] < State (2). A gram panchayat administers a cluster of villages, not a single village. Taluks contain multiple panchayats. Districts contain multiple taluks. Trap: Option B starts with Gram Panchayat before Village — a gram panchayat covers multiple villages so it is larger in administrative scope than a single village.

questions.stem: Arrange the following steps in correct order for judicial process in India: 1. Verdict, 2. Trial, 3. Filing of FIR, 4. Charge sheet, 5. Arrest. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Criminal justice sequence: Filing of FIR (3) → Arrest (5) → Charge sheet (4) [police investigation completed, charges filed before court] → Trial (2) [court proceedings] → Verdict (1). The FIR initiates the process; police may arrest after FIR; after investigation they file a charge sheet in court; then the trial happens; then the verdict. Trap: Option B puts arrest before FIR — while police can arrest in cognisable offences without FIR, the standard sequence for SSC reasoning purposes is FIR → arrest → charge sheet.

questions.stem: Arrange the following in descending order of wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum: 1. Gamma rays, 2. Visible light, 3. Radio waves, 4. X-rays, 5. Microwaves. Which sequence (longest to shortest) is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. EM spectrum from longest to shortest wavelength (ROYGBIV inward): Radio waves (3) > Microwaves (5) > Visible light (2) > X-rays (4) > Gamma rays (1). Mnemonic: Radio Micro Infra-red Visible Ultra-violet X-ray Gamma (RMIVUXG). Frequency is inverse of wavelength — radio waves have lowest frequency, gamma highest. Trap: Option B puts microwaves before radio waves — radio waves have wavelengths of metres to kilometres; microwaves are centimetres to millimetres; so radio waves are longer.

questions.stem: Arrange the following layers of the Earth from innermost to outermost: 1. Mantle, 2. Inner core, 3. Crust, 4. Outer core. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. From centre to surface: Inner core (2) → Outer core (4) → Mantle (1) → Crust (3). Inner core = solid iron-nickel ball (innermost). Outer core = liquid iron-nickel (surrounds inner core). Mantle = thick silicate rock layer (largest layer by volume). Crust = thin outermost layer (where we live). Trap: Option B starts with outer core before inner core — the inner core is at the centre; the outer core surrounds it. Option D puts outer core and mantle in wrong order.

questions.stem: Arrange the following stages of economic planning in India in chronological order: 1. New Economic Policy (LPG reforms), 2. Five Year Plans under Nehru, 3. Green Revolution, 4. NITI Aayog (replacing Planning Commission). Which is correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Chronological order: Five Year Plans under Nehru (2) — began 1951 → Green Revolution (3) — mid 1960s (high-yield seeds, 1965-1970) → New Economic Policy/LPG reforms (1) — 1991 (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) → NITI Aayog (4) — 2015 (replaced Planning Commission). Trap: Option B puts Green Revolution before Five Year Plans — Five Year Plans started 1951; Green Revolution happened in 1960s-70s within the plan framework. Option C puts LPG reforms (1991) before Green Revolution (1965) — wrong by 26 years.
